item.title: Explosiones interrumpen vuelos en Riad mientras se recrudece guerra entre Arabia Saudita y hutíes
item.description: Los hutíes de Yemen, alineados con Irán, intensificaron su letal campaña de ataques contra Riad, la capital de Arabia Saudita, donde el jueves se escucharon explosiones, se interrumpieron los vuelos y se ordenó a parte del personal de oficina que trabajara desde casa.
item.dc:creator: Timour Azhari
item.content:encoded: Los hutíes de Yemen, alineados con Irán, intensificaron su letal campaña de ataques contra Riad, la capital de Arabia Saudita, donde el jueves se escucharon explosiones, se interrumpieron los vuelos y se ordenó a parte del personal de oficina que trabajara desde casa. Los hutíes dijeron haber lanzado un misil balístico contra el aeropuerto de Riad y reiteraron su amenaza de forzar el cierre del espacio aéreo saudí después de que el reino prestó apoyo a las fuerzas del Gobierno yemení reconocido internacionalmente en una guerra civil que se ha reavivado. El conflicto, que ahora es una extensión de la guerra entre Estados Unidos e Irán, ha añadido caos a una región ya en llamas y amenaza con arrastrar a otros Estados a un agotador combate en las montañas, mientras Siria se plantea ahora desplegar tropas para ayudar a Arabia Saudita. El reino ha presionado para obtener el apoyo de naciones aliadas, entre ellas Turquía y Pakistán, aunque solo sea en el ámbito logístico o defensivo, mientras intenta revertir los avances hutíes en el suroeste de Yemen, junto a la entrada sur del mar Rojo. Esas peticiones han cobrado mayor urgencia desde que las autoridades saudíes anunciaron el miércoles que tres personas habían fallecido esta semana en ataques contra los aeropuertos de Riad y Abha, en el suroeste. LA GUERRA CIVIL SE REAVIVA A RAÍZ DEL CONFLICTO EN IRÁN El rastreador de vuelos FlightRadar24 indicó numerosos retrasos en las llegadas y salidas en el Aeropuerto Internacional Rey Khalid de Riad el jueves. Varias empresas multinacionales con sede en el Distrito Financiero Rey Abdullah (KAFD, por su sigla en inglés) de Riad ordenaron a su personal que trabajara desde casa tras las fuertes explosiones de la mañana del jueves, dijeron cinco personas familiarizadas con el asunto, entre ellas algunos empleados afectados. El Gobierno saudí no respondió a una solicitud de comentarios, y el KAFD no estuvo disponible de inmediato para hacer declaraciones. Algunos diplomáticos dijeron haber recibido alertas, y algunos colegios de Riad comunicaron a los padres que se habían recibido órdenes de permanecer en el interior, aunque las autoridades no emitieron ninguna alerta pública. Reuters no pudo identificar el origen de las explosiones. La prolongada guerra civil de Yemen, que se interrumpió con un alto el fuego en 2022, ha vuelto a estallar en las últimas semanas, tras la toma por parte de los hutíes el mes pasado de tramos de la costa del mar Rojo, incluidos algunos a lo largo del estratégico estrecho de Bab el-Mandeb. Los hutíes, que controlan muchas de las zonas más pobladas de Yemen, incluida la capital, Saná, han afirmado que estaban respondiendo a ataques del Gobierno respaldado por Arabia Saudita, algo que este último niega. Sus amenazas a la navegación por una vía marítima que se ha vuelto cada vez más crucial para las exportaciones de petróleo desde los ataques de Irán en el estrecho de Ormuz, así como sus ataques contra ciudades e infraestructuras saudíes, han llevado al reino a volver a intervenir. Esta semana, las fuerzas respaldadas por Arabia Saudita lanzaron un contraataque y recuperaron zonas en torno al estrecho. Sin embargo, en una guerra con varios frentes, los hutíes también han logrado avances, rodeando la tercera ciudad más grande de Yemen, Taiz, tras hacerse con el control de territorio a lo largo de su principal carretera de montaña hacia Adén. Los combates, que enfrentan a los hutíes contra una coalición de fuerzas respaldadas por Arabia Saudita bajo el mando del Gobierno reconocido internacionalmente, han provocado una crisis humanitaria en el Estado árabe más pobre, lo que ha provocado el desplazamiento de 200.000 personas desde que se reanudó el conflicto. AUTORIDADES DICEN QUE AYUDA SIRIA PODRÍA SER DEFENSIVA Un responsable de Defensa estadounidense y otro sirio dijeron que Siria estaba sopesando cuidadosamente las opciones de apoyo militar, incluida la ayuda defensiva para proteger a Arabia Saudita de los ataques, o un despliegue ofensivo para ayudar a llevar la lucha al territorio de los hutíes. En respuesta a una solicitud de comentarios dirigida al Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores sirio, un diplomático afirmó que Siria apoyaba firmemente a Arabia Saudita, pero que su atención se centraba en prioridades nacionales, como la recuperación de su propia guerra civil. Este verano boreal, Arabia Saudita firmó el Pacto de La Meca con Turquía y Pakistán, por el que los tres países se comprometen a defenderse mutuamente, aunque Ankara aún no ha ratificado el tratado. Turquía, miembro de la OTAN, dijo el miércoles que estaba enviando al reino apoyo principalmente defensivo y técnico para ayudar en la lucha contra los hutíes. Un funcionario turco señaló que se esperaba que este apoyo consistiera en equipamiento militar, intercambio de información de inteligencia y sistemas de armamento. Turquía, aliado cercano del Gobierno sirio y partidario de sus fuerzas cuando aún eran rebeldes que luchaban contra el Gobierno de Bashar al-Assad, ya había enviado anteriormente a algunos sirios a combatir en la guerra civil de Libia en 2020. Pakistán ha enviado por vía aérea equipamiento militar a Adén, en el sur de Yemen, para ayudar en la batalla contra los hutíes, según han indicado fuentes pakistaníes, y ha desplegado tropas en Arabia Saudita para ayudar a defender sus fronteras. Las autoridades saudíes y yemeníes no respondieron a las solicitudes de comentarios.

item.title: GlobalFoundries to make key AI chip component for TSMC in $2 billion deal
item.description: GlobalFoundries on Thursday said it has reached a $2 billion agreement to make a key component used to link AI processors and memory chips for TSMC at its New York facility.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: GlobalFoundries (GFS.O) on Thursday said it has reached a $2 billion agreement to make a key component used to link AI processors and memory chips for TSMC (2330.TW) at its New York facility. Known as a silicon interposer, the component sits beneath processors and memory chips inside advanced AI packages and enables them to communicate at high speeds. Under the five-year agreement, GlobalFoundries will expand manufacturing capacity at its Malta, New York, facility to produce the components for TSMC The Malta facility is expected to become the first US-based source of silicon interposers used in advanced chip-packaging technologies, the company said Shares of GlobalFoundries were up about 4% in premarket trading The deal provides a framework for future capacity expansion as demand for advanced packaging grows, with volume production expected to begin ramping up in the first half of 2028 Advanced packaging has become a major constraint on AI chip production, as demand for the technology exceeds available manufacturing capacity

item.title: POLL ECB to hike rates again in December as inflation almost doubles 2% target
item.description: The European Central Bank is expected to hold its deposit rate at 2.50% this month but raise it by 25 basis points in December as inflation runs nearly double its 2% target, a Reuters poll found. Most economists polled had until recently thought the ECB was done.
item.dc:creator: Indradip Ghosh
item.content:encoded: The European Central Bank is expected to hold its deposit rate at 2.50% this month but raise it by 25 basis points in December as [USN:L1N45O06O TEXT:"inflation runs nearly double its 2% target"], a Reuters poll found. Most economists polled had until recently thought the ECB was done. Global government bond yields have [USN:L4N45T14A TEXT:"climbed sharply"] over the past weeks, reflecting higher inflation expectations and fiscal worries. In Europe, investors [USN:L6N45O0HP TEXT:"have focused particularly on France"]. Caught between high inflation — at 3.8% in September and very close to the ECB's latest worst-case scenario — and concerns that rising yields could hurt growth, policymakers have recently argued for what ECB President Christine Lagarde called a "[USN:L8N45K12P TEXT:"measured response"]". So far there has been scant evidence that higher energy prices caused by the US-Israeli war with Iran are spilling into other consumer prices, which would be a trigger for more ECB rate rises. All but three of 73 economists polled October 5-8 expected the ECB to hold its 2.50% deposit rate on October 29, matching market pricing. The central bank raised rates for a second time this year in September. However, a near-90% majority of economists, 64 of 73, now see another hike in December. This marks a clear reversal from the over 90% expecting rates on hold in last month's survey. "Given uncertainties, the ECB is likely to remain on the current quarterly adjustment path and that should get us to another hike in December... the main risk is there may actually be one more hike, maybe in March," said Jens Eisenschmidt, chief Europe economist at Morgan Stanley. A 58% majority, 40 of 70, saw the deposit rate peaking at 2.75%. But over a third, 24, expect it to be 3.00%, up from just two last month. Markets are currently pricing nearly three hikes by end-2027. "I do not have a very strong conviction they go to 2.75% and stay there," said Eisenschmidt. "Our forecast is predicated on oil prices not increasing more and activity not accelerating further from here," he said. Inflation is expected to increase to 3.7% on average this quarter from 3.3% in the third quarter, higher than the 3.3% predicted last month, poll medians showed. It will average 3.0% and 2.6% this year and next, both upgrades from the 2.9% and 2.3% predicted last month. All policymakers agreed inflation risks were to the upside, the [USN:S8N42J027 TEXT:"accounts"] of the September 9-10 ECB meeting showed on Thursday. Meanwhile, [USN:ZRN00EN10 TEXT:"signs of stronger economic activity"] led to an upward revision to the growth outlook. The euro zone economy is expected to expand 1.0% this year, up from 0.8% in the previous survey. Growth is seen at 1.2% in 2027 and at 1.3% in 2028. ECB policymakers so far have argued against a rate rise at this month's meeting, even though the Middle East and Russia-Ukraine wars show no signs of abating just as the weather turns colder and demand for energy rises. The bond market selloff has also lowered expectations of an immediate increase. "A key argument against an October hike may be that market rates have increased meaningfully and are doing some of the job for the ECB," said Anatoli Annenkov, senior European economist at Societe Generale. ([USN:L6N45N0UX TEXT:"Other stories"] from the Reuters global economic poll)

item.title: US jobless claims hover near 57-year low for fourth consecutive week
item.description: The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits fell last week, pointing to continued labor market stability despite a sharp slowdown in job growth in September.
item.dc:creator: Lucia Mutikani
item.content:encoded: The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits fell last week, pointing to continued labor market stability despite a sharp slowdown in [USN:L1N45N170 TEXT:"job growth"] in September. Weekly jobless claims have now remained near 57-year lows for four straight weeks, the report from the Labor Department showed on Thursday, amid historically low layoffs. Though employers are hoarding workers against the backdrop of strong profit growth and stock market performance, they have remained hesitant to add to headcount, making it harder for those who lose their jobs to find new opportunities. Economists have blamed that trend on uncertainty, first from tariffs and then the US-Israeli war with Iran, which has pushed up diesel prices to record highs and boosted prices for other commodities. "It's still a 'low-hire, low-fire' job market," said Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union. "That's great for anyone who has a job and wants to keep it, but it's tough for job seekers." Initial claims for state unemployment benefits slipped 2,000 to a seasonally adjusted 197,000 for the week ended October 3, the Labor Department said. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast 200,000 claims for the latest week. Claims have held below the 200,000 mark since the second week of September. California and Illinois were the only states to report an increase in unadjusted applications in excess of 1,000. The four-week moving average of claims, viewed as a better gauge of labor market trends as it irons out week-to-week volatility, fell 2,500 to 198,000 last week, the lowest level since early October 2022. TEPID JOB GROWTH Nonfarm payrolls increased by a paltry 29,000 jobs in September, the government reported last week. Economists say tepid hiring and a shrinking labor pool amid retirements and an immigration crackdown are holding back job growth, leaving low layoffs to anchor the labor market. Minutes of the Federal Reserve's September 15-16 [USN:L6N45T0TQ TEXT:"policy meeting"], published on Wednesday, showed officials "judged that labor market conditions were stable and generally viewed the labor market as close to maximum employment." The minutes also noted that policymakers "generally viewed the upside and downside risks to the labor market as broadly balanced." The US central bank last month raised its [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"overnight benchmark interest rate"] by 25 basis points to the 3.75%-4.00% range, the first hike in three years, and flagged further increases in borrowing costs in the months ahead. The odds of another rate hike this month were diminished by the underwhelming payroll gains in September as well as cooler-than-expected [USN:L1N45M0L0 TEXT:"inflation readings"] for July and August. Economists expect the Fed to raise rates in December. The claims report showed the number of people receiving unemployment benefits after an initial week of aid, a proxy for hiring, increased 17,000 to a seasonally adjusted 1.716 million during the week ended September 26. The so-called continued claims had dropped to a 3-1/2-year low in the prior week. Some economists argued that the still-low level of continued claims was masking a gradual labor market weakening as a group of unemployed people, including recent college graduates, was ineligible for benefits because of limited or no work history. Some long-term unemployed people may have exhausted their eligibility, which is limited to 26 weeks in most states. The median duration of unemployment was 11.5 weeks in September, near a 4-1/2-year high. The unemployment rate was at 4.2% last month. "An ongoing rise in unemployment among new entrants and re-entrants to the labor market, amid weak hiring, will put some further gentle upward pressure on the unemployment rate over the next few quarters," said Samuel Tombs, chief US economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics.

item.title: US FDA flags four deaths in Newron's schizophrenia drug studies
item.description: Italy's Newron Pharmaceuticals said on Thursday the US FDA had identified four deaths among patients treated with its experimental schizophrenia drug in feedback following the agency's earlier decision to place a clinical hold on the treatment's trial in the US.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Italy's Newron Pharmaceuticals (NWRN.S) said on Thursday the US FDA had identified four deaths among patients treated with its experimental schizophrenia drug in feedback following the agency's earlier decision to place a clinical hold on the treatment's trial in the US. Shares of the Switzerland-listed company fell 5.7% in afternoon trading after the US Food and Drug Administration raised safety concerns, including the potential risk of irregular heart rhythms. Here are some details: The agency noted four deaths among patients who received evenamide across all studies, compared with one death among those given a placebo The FDA characterized the four deaths as a potential safety signal because a fatal arrhythmic mechanism could not be definitively excluded, Newron said. The drug was tested in people with treatment-resistant schizophrenia, a serious mental illness that affects thinking, emotions and perception of reality The feedback comes after the FDA earlier this year placed a clinical hold on new patient enrollment in a late-stage trial of evenamide following a patient's sudden death, although the event was unrelated to the treatment Newron said trial investigators considered three of the four deaths unrelated to evenamide. One was considered possibly related because two autopsies did not determine a cause of death The company said it has not identified a pattern of heart abnormalities or irregular rhythms in its preclinical and clinical safety data Newron is reviewing the FDA's feedback and the broader safety data generated across the evenamide development program and it plans to submit a response Newron said the clinical hold remains in place and enrollment in the trial is continuing outside the US

item.title: Spanish politicians trade blame after death of octogenarian at heart of housing protests
item.description: Maricarmen Abascal, 87, had been hospitalised for severe anxiety and exhaustion since her dramatic eviction last month.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Spanish politicians traded blame on Thursday after the [USN:L1N45T0T3 TEXT:"death of an 87-year-old woman"] who was evicted from her Madrid home exacerbated heated debates over housing ahead of an early election next month, as protests raged on across the country. Maricarmen Abascal, who died on Wednesday, had been hospitalised for severe anxiety and exhaustion since her [USN:L8N45F0PQ TEXT:"dramatic eviction"] on September 23, though no cause of death has been announced. News that she had died enraged protesters camped out on squares in Spain's main cities, who chanted that she had been "murdered" by the greed of her landlords. "When everything is private, we will be deprived of everything," said one placard on Madrid's Puerta del Sol square where mourners lit candles and left flowers honouring Maricarmen, as she has become known across Spain. Protests over housing shortages and surging rents sparked by Maricarmen's eviction prompted Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez to call a snap [USN:L8N45R05N TEXT:"general election"] on November 29. Following her death, political leaders were quick to invoke Maricarmen in their attacks on opponents. Left-leaning parties criticised the conservatives who had [USN:L1N45O0BD TEXT:"shot down decrees"] with housing measures aiming to curb soaring rental prices, while right-wingers said the leftist central government had proven unable to tackle the crisis after eight years in power. In the capital, Madrid, lawmakers accused each other of cynically exploiting Abascal's case. The conservative People's Party (PP), which has absolute majorities in the Madrid regional and local assemblies, refused to hold a minute of silence honouring Maricarmen, prompting hard-left deputies to stage one outside City Hall. They also gave her a 60-second standing ovation during a tense debate in the regional assembly, while PP lawmakers remained seated with folded arms. Madrid leader Isabel Diaz Ayuso of the PP blamed Sanchez, pointing out that the eviction had occurred under his government. Opposition leader Manuela Bergerot of the leftist Mas Madrid party said Maricarmen had died because of "miserable people who put gain above a person's life ... those responsible will carry that with them for their remaining days." She added that the last thing Ayuso had done while Maricarmen was alive was "laugh at her" — a reference to when Ayuso quipped on September 28: "At what age do I get to stop paying my landlords? Let me know."

item.title: Viatris to buy pain therapy maker Pacira BioSciences for $1.65 billion
item.description: Drugmaker Viatris will buy Pacira BioSciences for $1.65 billion in an all-cash deal, adding two non-opioid pain treatments to its portfolio, the companies said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Drugmaker Viatris (VTRS.O) will buy Pacira BioSciences (PCRX.O) for $1.65 billion in an all-cash deal, adding two non-opioid pain treatments to its portfolio, the companies said on Thursday. Viatris will pay $36.50 per share, a premium of 44.8% to the last closing price. Pacira's shares were up 44% in premarket trading. Pacira's non-opioid pain treatments, Exparel and Zilretta, generated sales of $575.1 million and $116.6 million, respectively, in 2025. Exparel is used to manage acute pain following surgery and Zilretta to treat pain associated with osteoarthritis of the knee. Viatris said it expects to expand the products' reach across select markets. The addition of the drugs is "synergistic with our fast-acting meloxicam market opportunity and position us as a leader in non-opioid pain management therapies," Viatris CEO Scott Smith said in a statement. The US FDA is expected to decide on approval for fast-acting meloxicam to treat moderate-to-severe acute pain by December 27. Viatris expects to fund the acquisition primarily with excess cash and the rest with short-term borrowings. The transaction would have minimal impact on its gross leverage ratio, it said. In August, Viatris [USN:L4N44315K TEXT:"raised"] its annual adjusted profit forecast, banking on strong branded drug sales and growth in China. The drugmaker has faced [USN:L4N3ZM181 TEXT:"manufacturing setbacks"] at its India operations, including a fire at its Nashik plant in western India, and mounting competition in generics, which have fueled concerns over growth and the resilience of its core business. The deal is expected to close by the end of 2026 and be immediately accretive to Viatris' financial guidance metrics, the company said.

item.title: Venture Global breached LNG supply deal with Galp, tribunal rules
item.description: Venture Global said on Thursday an arbitration tribunal found its Calcasieu Pass unit breached an LNG supply agreement with Portugal's Galp , marking the second setback for the firm over cargo deliveries from the project.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Venture Global (VG.N) said on Thursday an arbitration tribunal found its Calcasieu Pass unit breached an LNG supply agreement with Portugal's Galp (GALP.LS) , marking the second setback for the firm over cargo deliveries from the project. BP (BP.L) is the only other company to have prevailed in arbitration proceedings against Venture Global, as the US exporter deals with a string of disputes with long-term LNG buyers, which also includes Shell (SHEL.L) , Repsol (REP.MC) , Italy's Edison (EDNn.MI) and Poland's Orlen (PKN.WA) . The buyers accuse Venture Global of selling cargoes on the spot market at higher prices following Russia's invasion of Ukraine instead of delivering contracted volumes from initial production at the Louisiana plant. Venture Global has argued the spot sales were allowed as faulty power-island equipment delayed the start of commercial operations. The company said in its regulatory filing on Thursday that one of the three arbitrators at the International Chamber of Commerce tribunal dissented and that it is evaluating its options while continuing to defend its position. Remedies will be determined in a separate damages hearing expected in 2027 or 2028, with any final award subject to an aggregate seller liability cap of up to $170 million under the agreement, it added. The company also said the ruling does not affect the agreement currently being performed by the parties and noted it has delivered 20 cargoes to Galp since Calcasieu Pass reached commercial operations. After BP [USN:L3N3VQ1G3 TEXT:"won"] its arbitration case in 2025, Venture Global said in its annual report the British firm is seeking at least $3.7 billion in damages, though the claim could exceed $6 billion before interest, costs and fees. Venture Global has prevailed in separate arbitrations brought by [USN:L1N3U4117 TEXT:"Shell"] and [USN:L6N3YM1DM TEXT:"Repsol"], and subsequently defeated a court challenge related to that arbitration award. Italy's Edison [USN:L4N40E1PP TEXT:"settled"] its dispute earlier this year, with Venture Global agreeing to supply additional LNG cargoes beyond those required under their long-term contract.

item.title: China defends yuan policy as Europe steps up pressure over trade surplus
item.description: China pushed back against foreign criticism of its exchange-rate policy on Thursday, saying it has never pursued competitive depreciation, as European policymakers call for a stronger yuan to help curb China's record trade surplus and export surge.
item.dc:creator: Yukun Zhang, Kevin Yao
item.content:encoded: China pushed back against foreign criticism of its exchange-rate policy on Thursday, saying it has never pursued competitive depreciation, as European policymakers call for a stronger yuan to help curb China's record trade surplus and export surge. As China's trade surplus swells, European leaders have intensified calls for a stronger yuan, fearing a "China Shock 2.0" from a fresh wave of Chinese exports. In a lengthy policy statement, the People's Bank of China (PBOC) rejected claims that China keeps the yuan artificially weak to gain a trade advantage, as the EU's trade chief Maros Sefcovic is [USN:L6N45U0JM TEXT:"in Beijing"] to discuss [USN:L6N45T0P1 TEXT:"narrowing"] the bloc's trade deficit with China. "China neither needs nor intends to obtain a trade-competitive advantage through exchange-rate depreciation, and has never engaged in competitive currency depreciation," the central bank said. "Attributing a decline in domestic industrial competitiveness, the weakening of fiscal and financial discipline and complex structural problems simply to the exchange rates of other nations amounts to evading and shirking one's own responsibility for making necessary adjustments." China posted a record trade surplus of nearly $1.2 trillion in 2025, equivalent to about 6% of GDP, with analysts expecting exports of AI-related and other advanced technology products to help keep the surplus elevated this year. China's trade strength stems from the global competitiveness of its industries, the central bank said, arguing that countries with large trade surpluses have historically been those with strong manufacturing sectors. European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde in June [USN:L1N42U0R4 TEXT:"urged"] global leaders to discuss undervaluation of the Chinese currency as a facet of the imbalances endangering the global economy. The bloc is concerned about its trade imbalance with China, which reached €360.6 billion ($404 billion) in 2025, according to EU data, up 15% from the previous year. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has said the yuan is undervalued by 25% to 30% and called for a [USN:L8N43F0WI TEXT:"dialogue"] with China on monetary policy. Goldman Sachs said in August that the yuan is undervalued by at least 20% on some of its valuation models, arguing that a stronger currency would help narrow China's outsized trade and current-account surpluses and ease protectionist pressure from trading partners. The PBOC said exchange rates reflect multiple economic and financial factors, rejecting claims that isolated model estimates prove the yuan is undervalued. CHINA SAYS MARKET PLAYS DECISIVE ROLE The yuan has climbed about 4% against the dollar this year despite a widening US-China yield gap. The PBOC said the yuan has appreciated about 23% against the dollar since China's 2005 exchange-rate reform, strengthening from 8.27 yuan per dollar to around 6.7 currently. It warned that the yuan's outlook remains uncertain, with forces for both appreciation and depreciation shaping its trajectory. China lets the market play a decisive role in exchange-rate formation, the central bank said, adding that it does not preset exchange rate target levels or intervene in long-term exchange rate trends. "The People's Bank of China does not preset an exchange-rate target level, does not intervene in the long-term trend of the exchange rate, and maintains exchange-rate flexibility and two-way movement," it said. China will report additional foreign exchange-related data to the International Monetary Fund starting from 2027, the central bank said. The PBOC said China would pursue a domestic demand-led growth model under its 2026-2030 plan, boosting consumption, expanding effective investment and deepening high-level opening-up, while strengthening the domestic economy and helping drive a more balanced global economy. ($1 = 0.8937 euros)

item.title: Moroccan-Israeli defense firm MMI targets turret deliveries in March 2027
item.description: Moroccan Military Industry, a subsidiary of Israel's Elbit Systems, will begin delivering armoured vehicle turrets to the Moroccan army in March 2027, its general manager said, as Rabat pushes to build up its military industry with foreign partners.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Eljechtimi
item.content:encoded: Moroccan Military Industry, a subsidiary of Israel's Elbit Systems, will begin delivering armoured vehicle turrets to the Moroccan army in March 2027, its general manager said, as Rabat pushes to build up its military industry with foreign partners. Morocco and Israel, which resumed diplomatic ties in 2020, signed a defense cooperation pact in 2021, opening the way for collaboration in air defense, artillery, drones and defense manufacturing. MMI has a weapons systems facility in the Midparc industrial zone near Casablanca, while a second plant in Sidi Yahya, north of Rabat, is being established to manufacture medium and large-calibre ammunition, General Manager Kaduri Naor told Reuters on the sidelines of the Marrakech Air Show. The company has agreed with Morocco's defense administration to produce the turrets to be installed on 8x8 armoured vehicles assembled in Morocco by India's Tata, as well as related ammunition, Naor said. MMI is developing an anti-drone version of the same turret, targeting a rapidly growing global market as militaries seek lower-cost defenses against unmanned aerial threats, he said. "The threat is very cheap... defense systems are more expensive," he said, adding that MMI's solution was "cost-effective". The ammunition for the anti-drone turret will be produced in Morocco, equipped with a small radar that is designed to sense an incoming drone and trigger an explosion, dispersing tungsten fragments to destroy the target, he said. MMI is also planning to produce a self-propelled mortar system that can be mounted on vehicles, he said. The company hopes to use Morocco as a platform for exports, Naor said. "We will have a European NATO country to export to," he said, declining to identify the customer. Naor said 99% of MMI's staff, including engineers, were Moroccan.

item.title: Nobel/Littérature-Le prix décerné à la poète et écrivaine canadienne Anne Carson
item.description: Le prix Nobel de littérature a été décerné jeudi à la poète et écrivaine canadienne Anne Carson pour "son oeuvre audacieuse et inventive qui, dans un dialogue ludique avec la tradition classique, a créé de nouvelles formes pour la littérature contemporaine", a annoncé jeudi l'Académie royale des sciences de Suède.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le prix Nobel de littérature a été décerné jeudi à la poète et écrivaine canadienne Anne Carson pour "son oeuvre audacieuse et inventive qui, dans un dialogue ludique avec la tradition classique, a créé de nouvelles formes pour la littérature contemporaine", a annoncé jeudi l'Académie royale des sciences de Suède. Les lauréats du prix Nobel de littérature sont désignés par l'Académie royale des sciences de Suède. Le prix est accompagné d'un chèque de 12 millions de couronnes suédoises (1,07 million d'euros). "Elle a été très surprise. Nous n'avons pas eu beaucoup de temps pour parler et tout ce qu'elle a eu le temps de me dire, c’est qu'elle se trouve pour le moment en Islande, où elle écoute le vent", a déclaré Ingrid Carlberg, secrétaire permanente de l’Académie suédoise. Née à Toronto, Anne Carson possède également la nationalité islandaise depuis 2022 et a passé beaucoup de temps sur cette île arctique ces dernières années. L'oeuvre de la poète et essayiste canadienne Anne Carson mêle souvent vers, prose, dialogue et traduction dans un ensemble qui échappe aux classifications de genre. LITTÉRATURE GRECQUE CLASSIQUE Elle est notamment connue pour ses traductions de la littérature grecque classique, qui exerce une forte influence sur son oeuvre, qui comprend à la fois des livrets d'opéra et de la critique littéraire en passant par des romans en vers, comme "Autobiography of Red", paru en 1998. "Presque toute sa production littéraire s'est construite autour de l'intersection entre l'obsession du philologue pour les mots et le désir du poète de leur donner un sens nouveau", a déclaré l’Académie. "Elle a elle-même identifié l'étymologie des mots comme le point de départ de toute son œuvre. Ses traductions du grec ancien peuvent être considérées comme des œuvres à part entière." Son style se retrouve notamment dans Norma Jeane Baker of Troy, une œuvre scénique créée en 2019 qui entrelace le mythe d’Hélène de Troie - tel qu'évoqué dans la tragédie d'Euripide "Hélène" - et le destin de Marilyn Monroe, Norma Jeane étant le vrai prénom de l'icône hollywoodienne. L'Académie a également salué sa capacité à explorer "les possibilités de l’écriture, un processus par lequel l’esquisse littéraire a pris une importance particulière à ses yeux". "En témoigne notamment "Float" (2016), une euuvre composée de 22 courts livrets consacrés à différents sujets, qui peuvent être lus dans n’importe quel ordre", a-t-elle déclaré. SANS PROUST Souvent présenté comme son œuvre majeure, "Autobiography of Red" témoigne de la capacité d'Anne Carson à "actualiser la tradition littéraire classique", a déclaré l’Académie. Dans cet ouvrage, elle réexamine des questions séculaires telles que: "Que se passe-t-il lorsque l’on aime quelqu’un qui finira par vous détruire?" Puisant dans des sources d'inspiration plus contemporaines, Anne Carson s'est penchée sur le personnage d’Albertine, l’une des figures féminines centrales d’"À la recherche du temps perdu" de Marcel Proust, dans son propre ouvrage "The Albertine Workout". Anne Carson avait consacré sept ans à la lecture du chef-d’œuvre de Marcel Proust et avait déclaré dans une interview accordée à CBC Radio One en 2016 qu’elle avait ressenti des symptômes de sevrage après avoir terminé le livre, ce qui l’avait conduite à écrire "The Albertine Workout" pour prolonger l’expérience. "On pense que la vie continue après Proust, mais elle semble tellement grise", avait-elle déclaré. PARKINSON Anne Carson a commencé à prendre des cours de boxe alors qu’elle avait déjà dépassé 70 ans, après avoir été diagnostiquée de la maladie de Parkinson. Ce sport est recommandé comme thérapie, notamment parce qu’il aide à travailler la coordination entre les mains et les yeux ainsi que l’enchaînement des mouvements. Elle a évoqué les effets de la maladie sur son écriture manuscrite lors d’un entretien au Louisiana Literary Festival, au Danemark, en 2024: "J'efface des paragraphes entiers, par honte (...) la honte d’avoir une mauvaise écriture." Anne Carson, qui a enseigné les lettres classiques dans des universités au Canada et aux États-Unis, a déclaré qu’elle se considérait autant comme une artiste visuelle que comme une écrivaine. "Je conçois la création d’un poème comme la création d’un objet. J’ai toujours considéré mes poèmes davantage comme des dessins que comme des textes, mais des dessins dans lesquels on peut aussi entrer physiquement grâce au langage", avait-elle déclaré dans son entretien à CBC. CARSON PARMI LES FAVORITES CETTE ANNÉE Âgée de 76 ans, Anne Carson figurait parmi les favorites pour le prix de cette année, selon les bookmakers de Ladbrokes. Anne Carson rejoint des figures majeures telles qu’Alexandre Soljenitsyne, Alice Munro - une autre Canadienne, lauréate en 2013 - et Ernest Hemingway parmi les lauréats du prix, qui suscite régulièrement des débats dans le monde littéraire. L'Académie a été vivement critiquée pour avoir ignoré certains des géants de la littérature des 120 dernières années, comme Léon Tolstoï, Virginia Woolf ou encore Jorge Luis Borges. Elle a également été accusée de délaisser les auteurs américains récemment - même si elle a décerné le prix à l’auteur-compositeur-interprète Bob Dylan en 2016 et récompensé la poétesse Louise Glück en 2020 - ainsi que de privilégier des choix jugés trop obscurs. Ses défenseurs soulignent que l'Académie a aussi récompensé des auteurs devenus très populaires, comme le Colombien Gabriel García Márquez en 1982 et la Britannique Doris Lessing en 2007. Ils estiment par ailleurs que la mission de l'Académie consiste notamment à mettre en lumière des traditions littéraires moins connues et à encourager les lecteurs à élargir leurs horizons. LES PRIX CRÉÉS PAR LE TESTAMENT DE L'INVENTEUR SUÉDOIS Les cinq prix Nobel originels ont été créés conformément aux dispositions du testament d'Alfred Nobel, inventeur et industriel suédois dont la fortune provenait notamment de l'invention de la dynamite. Ils sont décernés depuis 1901, avec seulement quelques interruptions, principalement pendant la Première et la Seconde Guerre mondiale. Un sixième prix, celui d'économie, a été institué en 1968 par la banque centrale suédoise, la Riksbank. Le prix de littérature de [USN:L5N3VQ0T1 TEXT:"l’année dernière"] a été décerné à l'écrivain et scénariste hongrois Laszlo Krasznahorkai, qualifié de "maître de l'apocalypse" par la critique américaine Susan Sontag. Ce prix est le quatrième prix annoncé cette année, conformément à la tradition, après ceux de [USN:L8N45R118 TEXT:"médecine"] lundi, de [USN:S8N43900O TEXT:"physique"] mardi et de [USN:L8N45T0LN TEXT:"chimie"] mercredi. Suivront ces prochains jours les annonces des prix Nobel de la paix (vendredi) et de l'économie (lundi prochain).

item.title: Morocco aerospace exports could rise to $5 billion, industry group says
item.description: Morocco's aerospace industry could increase annual exports to about $5 billion within three years from $3 billion last year, as it attracts new suppliers manufacturing high-value parts, the head of industry association GIMAS said.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Eljechtimi
item.content:encoded: Morocco's aerospace industry could increase annual exports to about $5 billion within three years from $3 billion last year, as it attracts new suppliers manufacturing high-value parts, the head of industry association GIMAS said. The North African country's aerospace sector employs about 25,000 people across around 160 companies, including suppliers to Airbus (AIR.PA) , Boeing (BA.N) and Safran (SAF.PA) . The sector aims to increase local value added by moving beyond producing individual components into manufacturing more complex aerospace systems, GIMAS head Mohammed Bellatig told Reuters on the sidelines of the Marrakech Airshow. He said that in the near future, Morocco would be assembling engines and landing gear "so that we provide much bigger added value than we have today". French defence group Safran is currently expanding its footprint in the country by building plants to produce aircraft [USN:L8N3Z920A TEXT:"landing gear"] and [USN:L5N3VU1EF TEXT:"Airbus jet engines"]. Morocco is also looking to gain a foothold in the drone industry, which officials view as a natural extension of capabilities already developed in aircraft manufacturing. Bellatig said drone production could leverage expertise in materials, assembly and engineering already present in the country's aerospace sector. The push received further support at the October 7-10 Marrakech Air Show, where Morocco signed a memorandum of understanding with French defense startup Harmattan AI to manufacture Moroccan autonomous drones designed for deep-strike missions at ranges of up to 2,000 km, with key technologies to be developed and produced locally. In recent years, Moroccan authorities have granted licences to a series of local and foreign-backed drone projects, with involvement from companies including Turkish Baykar, producer of Bayraktar TB2.

item.title: Genre-defying Canadian poet Anne Carson wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
item.description: Canadian poet and writer Anne Carson, whose work often blends verse, prose, dialogue and translation in a genre-defying mix, won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature on Thursday for what the Swedish Academy called her "bold and inventive oeuvre".
item.dc:creator: Johan Ahlander, Stine Jacobsen, Justyna Pawlak
item.content:encoded: Canadian poet and writer Anne Carson, whose work often blends verse, prose, dialogue and translation in a genre-defying mix, won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature on Thursday for what the Swedish Academy called her "bold and inventive oeuvre". "Crazy, I think they're all crazy," Carson told Icelandic broadcaster RUV when asked how she was feeling after learning she had won while on the Arctic island. "I'll get a sticker on the front of my book." Carson, 76, who was born in Toronto and has a home in Iceland, had been taken by surprise when called with the news, said Ingrid Carlberg, permanent secretary of the Academy, which awards the prize worth 12 million Swedish crowns ($1.2 million). "All she had time to tell me was that she is for the moment in Iceland, where she's listening to the wind," Carlberg told a press conference in Stockholm after the announcement. She is widely known for her translations of classical Greek literature, which heavily influences her work that ranges from opera libretti to literary criticism and verse novels such as "Autobiography of Red" from 1998. 'NEW FORMS OF CONTEMPORARY LITERATURE' In its citation, the Swedish Academy said it was recognising Carson "for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature". "Almost all her literary production has centred upon the intersection between the philologist's obsession with words and the poet's desire for new meaning," the Academy said. "She has herself identified the etymology of words as the starting point for all her work. Her translations from Classical Greek may be regarded as independent works in their own right." Her style is exemplified in "Norma Jeane Baker of Troy" from 2019, a performance piece which mixes the stories of Helen of Troy in Euripides' play "Helen" with Marilyn Monroe. The Academy also praised her ability to explore "the possibilities of writing, a process by which the literary sketch has become of particular value to her". "Bearing witness to this is Float (2016), a work consisting of 22 chapbooks on different subjects, capable of being read in any order," it said. LIFE WITHOUT PROUST Often heralded as her greatest work, "Autobiography of Red" demonstrates Carson's ability to "actualise the classical literary tradition", the Academy said. In the book, she re-examines age-old questions such as "What happens when you love someone who will ultimately destroy you?" Tapping into more modern inspirations, Carson reflected on the character of Albertine, one of the narrator Marcel's love interests in Marcel Proust's "In Search of Lost Time", in her own book "The Albertine Workout". Carson had spent seven years reading Proust's masterpiece and said in an interview with Canada's CBC Radio One in 2016 that she suffered withdrawal symptoms after finishing, leading her to write "The Albertine Workout" as a way to prolong the experience. "You think life goes on after Proust, but it seems so grey," she said. BOXING LESSONS TO FIGHT PARKINSON'S Carson started taking boxing lessons when she was already in her 70s because of a Parkinson's disease diagnosis. The sport is recommended as a therapy because it helps pay attention to hand-eye coordination and the sequencing of actions. She reflected on the disease's impact on her handwriting in an interview at the Louisiana Literary Festival in Denmark in 2024: "I scrub out whole paragraphs in shame ... the shame of bad handwriting." Carson, who has taught classics at universities in Canada and the United States, has said that she considers herself a visual artist as much as a literary one. "I think of making a poem as making an object. I have always thought of them more as drawings than as texts, but drawings that are also physically enterable through the fact of language," she said in the CBC interview. Poetry, she says, may be more attuned to the fast modern-day life than long-form writing. "I think it's probably more useful than prose right now because it's faster and everybody is in a hurry so basically it's good because it is brief," she told the Icelandic broadcaster on Thursday. 'AT HOME' IN ICELAND AND NYC Carson and her husband, artist Robert Currie, first came to Iceland after the 2008 banking collapse and gradually spent more time there. "We got to know people and we liked the people," Carson told Iceland Review in 2023. She has held citizenship of Iceland since 2022. Currie told the magazine Iceland was one of only two places that immediately felt like home to him, the other being New York City in the 1970s. Literature was the fourth of this year's Nobels to be announced this week, following [USN:L1N45R0AK TEXT:"medicine"], [USN:L1N45S0E6 TEXT:"physics"] and [USN:L1N45T09K TEXT:"chemistry"]. The peace prize winner will be announced in Oslo on Friday. Established in the will of Swedish dynamite inventor and businessman Alfred Nobel, the prizes have been awarded since 1901. Carson, who had been among the favourites this year, takes a place beside luminaries such as Alexander Solzhenitsyn, Alice Munro and Ernest Hemingway as a recipient of the award. Last year's prize was won by Hungarian writer [USN:L2N3VQ0DK TEXT:"Laszlo Krasznahorkai"]. ($1 = 10.0190 Swedish crowns)

item.title: Camera dei Deputati approva nuova legge elettorale
item.description: La Camera ha approvato in via definitiva una nuova legge elettorale sostenuta dalla presidente del Consiglio Giorgia Meloni e duramente contestata dalle opposizioni, che potrebbe avere un ruolo chiave nell'esito delle elezioni previste il prossimo anno.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La Camera ha approvato in via definitiva una nuova legge elettorale sostenuta dalla presidente del Consiglio Giorgia Meloni e duramente contestata dalle opposizioni, che potrebbe avere un ruolo chiave nell'esito delle elezioni previste il prossimo anno. Meloni sostiene che le nuove regole sono pensate per aumentare la prospettiva di un governo stabile. L'opposizione di centrosinistra afferma che l'obiettivo sia rafforzare le sue possibilità di mantenere il potere. In una votazione segreta, i parlamentari hanno approvato con 227 voti favorevoli e 164 contrari un disegno di legge che introduce un sistema elettorale interamente proporzionale, con un premio di maggioranza per qualsiasi coalizione che ottenga più del 42% dei voti. "CHI VINCE DEVE POTER GOVERNARE" "Introduciamo regole pensate per favorire la stabilità e la coerenza parlamentare di qualunque governo, indipendentemente dal suo colore politico", ha scritto Meloni su X dopo il voto. "Perché chi vince le elezioni deve poter governare". Quando la riforma fu concepita, il blocco di destra guidato da Meloni era in testa nei sondaggi e i critici sostenevano che le modifiche fossero state studiate per garantirle una solida maggioranza dopo le elezioni. Tuttavia, il panorama politico è cambiato da quando a febbraio è emerso il nuovo partito di estrema destra Futuro Nazionale guidato da Roberto Vannacci, che ha eroso il consenso dei partiti di governo. Gli ultimi sondaggi mostrano la coalizione di governo dietro al centrosinistra e alcuni analisti ritengono che la riforma potrebbe addirittura ritorcersi contro Meloni, il cui esecutivo ha celebrato il mese scorso quasi quattro anni al potere, diventando il più longevo in Italia dalla Seconda Guerra Mondiale. Nel corso di un acceso dibattito, i parlamentari del centrosinistra hanno accusato il governo di calpestare la democrazia imponendo le nuove regole alla vigilia delle elezioni e contro la volontà dell'opposizione. "Cambiatevi pure da soli questa legge elettorale, perché tanto noi saremo in grado con la nostra alleanza progressista di vincere con qualunque legge elettorale", ha dichiarato la segretaria del Partito Democratico Elly Schlein. Uno degli elementi della riforma obbliga ogni coalizione, o ogni partito che si presenta da solo, a indicare il proprio candidato premier prima delle elezioni. Questo mette il centrosinistra in una situazione difficile, poiché i leader di PD e Movimento 5 Stelle sono in disaccordo su chi dovrebbe assumere la guida del governo in caso di vittoria dell'alleanza. TENSIONI NELLA COALIZIONE L'approvazione definitiva della riforma ha richiesto quattro votazioni parlamentari e ha posto fine a mesi di tensioni interne alla maggioranza che avevano alimentato dubbi sulla capacità di Meloni di mantenere compatta la propria alleanza in vista delle elezioni del prossimo anno. Le tensioni riguardavano in particolare la reintroduzione delle preferenze per la scelta degli eletti, ma alla fine è stato raggiunto un compromesso con il capolista che resta bloccato. "E a chi sperava di vedere il centrodestra diviso, oggi rispondiamo con i fatti: siamo uniti, compatti e determinati a portare avanti gli impegni presi con i cittadini", ha affermato Meloni.

item.title: Wall St slips as higher yields and oil prices flag inflation risk
item.description: US stocks edged lower on Thursday as soaring oil prices and Treasury yields near multi-year highs stoked inflation worries on the cusp of a critical earnings season expected to test recent market gains.
item.dc:creator: Tharuniyaa Lakshmi, Shashwat Chauhan
item.content:encoded: US stocks edged lower on Thursday as soaring oil prices and Treasury yields near multi-year highs stoked inflation worries on the cusp of a critical earnings season expected to test recent market gains. Brent crude futures jumped 4.2% to more than $104 a barrel on [USN:L1N45U031 TEXT:"persistent worries"] about supply from the Middle East after increasing attacks on shipping in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz. The bond market rout showed no sign of abating as the yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury bond stood at 5.29%, close to its highest mark since 2002. Risk assets around the world took a hit on Thursday. Megacap growth stocks were broadly lower, with Amazon.com (AMZN.O) , Tesla (TSLA.O) and Nvidia (NVDA.O) down between 0.3% and 1.3%. Chip-related companies also eased, with Marvell Technology (MRVL.O) and Intel (INTC.O) losing about 3% apiece and AMD (AMD.O) down 2%. Forecasts of record quarterly profit from memory-chip giant Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) failed to [USN:L1N45T115 TEXT:"lift sentiment"] and its shares closed lower in South Korea. Rival Micron Technology (MU.O) dropped 1.4%. Meanwhile, the Wall Street Journal [USN:FWN45T25Y TEXT:"report"]ed on Wednesday that Broadcom (AVGO.O) is lining up $50 billion of financing for OpenAI, with Oracle (ORCL.N) also seeking an unspecified sum, spurring fears that massive debt issuance by technology companies could intensify the competition for capital. Broadcom and Oracle were trading lower amid wider weakness in tech stocks. A rebound in Treasury yields and oil prices knocked the S&P 500 (.SPX) and the Nasdaq (.IXIC) from record highs a day earlier, while the Dow snapped a four-day winning streak. "We've got dueling headwinds with energy prices and Treasury yields and light on the economic data front, kind of a wait and see on earnings which really kick off in earnest next week," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth. Eight out of 11 S&P 500 sectors traded lower, with the technology (.SPLRCT) and healthcare (.SPXHC) indexes losing the most. Energy (.SPNY) and consumer staples (.SPLRCS) were leading gains, rising about 2% and 1%, respectively, while utilities (.SPLRCU) was marginally higher. At 09:43 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) fell 88.19 points, or 0.17%, to 51,096.19, the S&P 500 (.SPX) lost 28.08 points, or 0.36%, to 7,773.69, and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) shed 155.07 points, or 0.58%, to 27,383.62. WALL STREET AWAITS EARNINGS Big banks including JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) are due to report results next week. Optimism around strong earnings has buoyed US stocks lately despite shaky geopolitical developments and concerns about rising interest rates. The technology and energy sectors are expected to report the biggest quarterly earnings growth, while the broader S&P 500 (.SPX) is expected to post a 30.6% increase in quarterly earnings, according to data compiled by LSEG. US [USN:L6N45T15S TEXT:"Federal Reserve"] Governor Christopher Waller hinted at a possible pause at the central bank's upcoming meeting. Additional rate hikes would likely be needed to lower inflation to the Fed's 2% target, but there was "flexibility" about the pace of increases, he said earlier in the day. Traders widely expect the Fed to hold rates steady at its October meeting, but a December hike is still on the cards, according to CME FedWatch. In individual movers, Wolfspeed (WOLF.N) soared 9.6% after the chipmaker received a $1.5 billion [USN:L6N45T187 TEXT:"conditional loan"] commitment from the US Department of Defense. PepsiCo (PEP.O) cut its annual [USN:L6N45U0N9 TEXT:"core profit forecast"] and said it would pursue additional spending cuts. Its shares rose 2.1%. Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.64-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 2.53-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 posted 3 new 52-week highs and 12 new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 13 new highs and 128 new lows.

item.title: Germany's Uniper sale risks leaving money on table
item.description: Berlin is re-privatising the energy group, which it rescued in a €14 bln 2022 bailout. Its ambition to keep the company’s disparate parts under one roof rests on shaky logic about energy security. But a breakup would be a far more lucrative strategy for taxpayers.
item.dc:creator: Liam Proud
item.content:encoded: When Germany rescued Uniper (UN0k.DE) in 2022, making a profit wasn't the priority. The goal was to stabilise a company that was, and still is, central to the energy needs of Europe's largest economy. Now, as Berlin re-privatises Uniper, it could in theory more than break even. But insisting on keeping the disparate portfolio of businesses together risks a discounted valuation. Uniper is one of those companies that no one would invent if it didn't already exist. It spans Swedish nuclear power, German gas-fired plants, an energy-trading unit and other businesses. When Russia invaded Ukraine it suffered two blows. Uniper faced collateral demands on derivative trades, and when Russian gas was no longer flowing it had to pay exorbitant prices for replacement supplies. Berlin stepped in with €13.5 billion of capital injections , and bought shares from the group's then-controlling Finnish owner Fortum (FORTUM.HE) for around €500 million. That left the government with a 99% stake. Now it's time to get out. Officially, the government is pursuing two options: either a majority sale or an initial public offering, retaining a 25% holding in either scenario. Floating looks tough given a subdued European market, which means the roughly 75% stake sale seems more likely. Reuters has [USN:L8N45S0FP TEXT:"reported"] that the runners and riders in the bidding include Apollo Global Management (APO.N) , Norway's Equinor (EQNR.OL) , Daniel Kretinsky's EPH, and two consortia. One pairs KKR (KKR.N) and Germany's RWE (RWEG.DE) and another involves Brookfield and the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board. On paper, a breakup is the best way to maximise value. Nordic players would probably go for the assets in their home region, while RWE or buyout barons could take the local German generation business, for example. It's hard to know what these parties would bid, but one way to think about the possible breakup value is to use brokers' sum-of-the-parts valuations. ODDO BHF analysts value Uniper's equity at €17.7 billion, after adding up the value of its component parts, including net cash and deducting other liabilities. On that basis, the government could bank a tidy profit based on the paper value of its holding - especially since it has already received around €3.5 billion from Uniper, through state aid paybacks and dividends, according to Reuters. But the chances of taxpayers seeing that much value seems remote. That's because Berlin wants to keep a one-quarter stake to retain influence over major decisions, and appears to oppose a breakup, meaning Uniper will merit a hefty conglomerate discount. A finance ministry spokesperson said Berlin wants to ensure the viability of the company as a whole, given its importance to country's energy supply. That doesn't seem like a great argument. First, Swedish nuclear power has little to do with German energy security. As for the local assets, governments have many ways to influence producers without owning large stakes, including through regulation. Saving Uniper wasn't about making a profit, but that doesn't mean Berlin has to leave money on the table. Follow Liam Proud on Bluesky and LinkedIn . Apollo Global Management has submitted a non-binding offer for Uniper, Reuters reported on October 7, citing two people with direct knowledge of the matter. Potential suitors had until September 21 to submit indicative bids for the German state-owned energy firm, which was taken over by the German government in 2022 under a €13.5 billion ($15.1 billion) bailout. In total, Berlin has received around €3.5 billion from Uniper since the bailout, including state aid paybacks and dividends. Norway's Equinor, and a consortium consisting of KKR with German utility RWE, have also submitted bids, Reuters reported citing one of the two people. Suitors are expected to be informed about whether they can proceed to the next round in the coming weeks, according to the report, which cited a third person involved in the talks. item.title: Morning Bid: Wall Street winces at bond squeeze
item.description: Stock markets finally stalled on Wednesday and early Thursday as the bond crunch ground on, with the latest Federal Reserve minutes showing most policymakers in September saw more interest rate rises ahead.
item.dc:creator: Mike Dolan
item.content:encoded: Stock markets [USN:L6N45T0JD TEXT:"finally stalled"] on Wednesday and early [USN:L4N45T1LT TEXT:"Thursday"] as the bond crunch ground on, with the latest Federal Reserve minutes [USN:L6N45T0TQ TEXT:"showing"] most policymakers in September saw more interest rate rises ahead. Markets have scaled back the Fed tightening horizon a bit in recent weeks but still see three more hikes over the coming year, starting in December. Reinforcing the message from the Fed minutes, Fed Governor Christopher Waller [USN:L6N45T15S TEXT:"said on Thursday"] that additional rate hikes will likely be needed to lower inflation to the Fed's 2% target - although he said there was "flexibility" about the pace. There was [USN:L8N45T0F3 TEXT:"some relief"] in bond land on Wednesday after the latest 10-year Treasury auction went off OK, but not before yields hit another 24-year high earlier in the day. There are 30-year bonds up for grabs later on Thursday too. While Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has downplayed the latest bond moves as global rather than US-specific, the so-called "term premium" in 10-year debt that accounts for investor uncertainty beyond Fed interest rates has risen again to its highest in 12 years. Having set new records earlier in the week, Wall Street stocks [USN:L6N45T0JD TEXT:"pulled back"] on Wednesday, with the focus shifting to the upcoming earnings season and the latest round of circular financing in the AI world between chipmakers and their customers. Reports overnight detailed the latest debt financing between Broadcom and OpenAI, following reports this week that SpaceX and Nvidia [USN:L6N45S1CQ TEXT:"are arranging"] chip finance of up to $40 billion. Broadcom and Anthropic too are discussing debt financing on a similar scale. The rise of debt in the AI buildout, and what appears to some like "vendor financing", raises the stakes for earnings season updates on the durability of the boom. Taiwan chip giant TSMC's quarterly revenue once again [USN:P8N3NB03R TEXT:"beat lofty forecasts"] on Thursday, while South Korea's Samsung underlined the scale of things there as it [USN:P8N44T045 TEXT:"reported"] a more than 700% annual rise in operating profit. Yet even that [USN:L4N45T1LT TEXT:"wasn't enough"] for the market, which knocked Samsung shares down more than 1% on some indications that the pace of growth and chip price rises were set to cool. Chart of the day The so-called term premium on 10-year US Treasury yields, the added compensation for risk demanded by investors for holding the bond to maturity, rose this week to its highest level since 2014, according to the New York Fed's model. The climb in nominal Treasury borrowing rates to 24-year highs over recent months has mostly been attributed to a rethink of the Fed's interest rate horizon, and this has been reflected in the rise of real inflation-adjusted yields. Long-term inflation expectations have remained relatively stable. But the spike in the term premium reflects broader concerns about rising debt levels, political risks and the uncertainties surrounding government financing over the longer term.
